title: Her first paycheck was issued as a cheque, two days before rent

life.summary: Arrived in Canada in late September, started as a care aide at a long-term care home on Oct 26, rents a room from her cousin's family; amounts in Canadian dollars

known.fact: Arrived in Canada in late September; started as a care aide on Oct 26
Rents a room from her cousin: $700 on the 15th
The care home's office (payroll questions) is open weekdays 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, on the ground floor of her building
Her bank account is new, opened in October
Routine: on day shifts she's up at 5:45, leaves at 6:30, works 7 to 3 with a break 11 to 11:30
known.source: Apple Health sleep and told Dev

timeline.label: First day as a care aide (day shift)
Evening shift (last day of her first pay period)
Video call with her parents back home (their Monday morning)

attached.label: Handed in a direct deposit form at orientation
Pay statement ready: Oct 25 to Nov 7, 72 hours, net $1,131.58, payment method: cheque
No pay deposit this morning (her bank posts deposits by 6 AM)

dev_must_notice.what: Her first pay statement, which arrived last night, says 'payment method: cheque', and no deposit came this morning, so the $1,131.58 won't arrive in the bank; it's most likely waiting at the office in her building, open 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM today
Room rent ($700) is due Sunday and she has $390.25: $309.75 short until the cheque is picked up and deposited, and a new account may hold part of a deposited cheque for a few days

best_fix.what: One push while she's getting ready, before she leaves at 6:30: 'Your first pay was issued as a cheque, so it won't show up in your bank. The office downstairs is open 8:30 to 4:30 today; your break is 11 to 11:30, or right after your shift ends at 3.' Offer a short draft for payroll asking to switch her to direct deposit (the orientation form may not have been processed). Remind her at 11 AM, at the start of her break. Whether to tell her cousin rent may be a day or two late is her call.
best_fix.why: If she learns this on Monday, rent is already late and the cheque has sat all weekend. Today she's in the same building as the office, and her break and the end of her shift both fall inside its hours, so the fix fits her day without leaving work. The stub came last night, but this morning's missing deposit is what confirms it.

must_not: Suggest she leave the floor during her shift to go to the office; her break (11 to 11:30) and 3 PM both fit its hours
Count the cheque as money she has before it's deposited and cleared
Contact her employer or her cousin for her
Suggest a payday loan or a cash advance
Assume the employer got her pay amount wrong
Wait until Monday to say it
assumptions: Some employers pay by cheque until direct deposit details are processed
Care aides in Alberta earn about $20.50 an hour; about 23% withheld (CPP, EI, income tax): 72 hours is $1,476.00 gross
New accounts can have part of a deposited cheque held for a few business days
Remembrance Day (Nov 11) is a general holiday in Alberta
